highlight.title: Go live from your browser — no OBS needed
highlight.text: Press Go Live, allow your camera and microphone, and you're live, with your own channel and chat. There's nothing to install and no follower or subscriber minimum. It works on a Chromebook, a laptop or a phone.
points: No OBS, plug-ins or capture card: WebRTC in the browser, with under a second of delay

Share your screen, a window or a tab, with your camera over it
When you want scenes, use OBS or any RTMP or WHIP encoder

faq: What is OpenRestream?
An open restreaming platform at openre.stream: you send one stream from OBS or any RTMP encoder, and it forwards it to every platform you add, plus your OpenVibe Live channel by default.
Is OpenVibe Live on by default?
Yes. A new stream also goes live on your openvibe.live channel, with chat, clips and VODs. You can switch that off for any stream, and your other destinations keep working.
Does it cost anything?
No. Restreaming is free for every OpenVibe account, and the code is open source.
Can I stream without OBS?
Yes. Go live from your browser on OpenVibe.Live: press Go Live, allow your camera and microphone, and you are live. There is nothing to install.
Do I need followers or subscribers to go live?
No. Every OpenVibe account can go live from the first minute, with no follower, subscriber or past-stream requirement.
Can I stream from a Chromebook or a phone?
Yes. The broadcaster runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on ChromeOS, Android and iOS as well as Windows, macOS and Linux.
Can I restream to Twitch, YouTube and Kick at the same time?
Yes. One broadcast can go to Twitch, YouTube, Kick and any RTMP, RTMPS or SRT server at once.
Can I use OBS if I want to?
Yes. OBS and any RTMP encoder work, and so do WHIP encoders (OBS 30 and later, ffmpeg, GStreamer).

faq: Is it free?
Yes. Searching for food and reading the food list need no account; a free OpenVibe account keeps your plans and your cupboard.
Where do the food banks and stores come from?

From OpenStreetMap, the map anyone can edit, under the Open Database License. Every result is credited and links to its OpenStreetMap entry, and answers are cached for a week so OpenStreetMap is asked politely.
Are the prices live?
No. The food list carries typical prices from budget chains, and every price says so. Live delivery and store prices come with the comparison feature.
How does the meal planner work?
Tell it how many people, how many days and, if you like, a budget. It picks budget foods that cover each food group, splits the shopping by the cheapest store and lays out a menu for each day.
Is the cupboard advice dietary advice?
No. It matches what you have against simple recipes written by OpenVibe and says which ones you can make now and which need one or two more things.

faq: How does Quest know what I did?

The OpenVibe sites already report events such as a stream starting or a thread being posted. Quest counts the ones its quests name, for the person each event names, and nothing else: no page views, no clicks, nothing you wrote.
What do quests pay?
A badge for each completed quest, shown on your profile across the network. OpenCoins rewards are built and switch on soon.
Are OpenCoins money?
No. OpenCoins are loyalty points for the OpenVibe network. They are never money, and Quest never pays in Vibes.
Can my community make its own quests?
Not yet: community quests need moderation tools first. The quest log and its API are already built for them.

faq: Who posts the listings?
People with an OpenVibe account. In this first version nothing is copied from other listing sites; sources whose terms allow it come later, each named and linked.
Does OpenVibe take payments or deposits?
No. A listing carries a way to contact the person who posted it and nothing more. Never pay or send a deposit before you have seen the place and signed an agreement.
Why can't I add my street address?
For your safety: a listing names a city and, if you like, a neighbourhood. A street address is refused.
How long does a listing stay up?
Thirty days. You can renew it, edit it, hide it or delete it at any time.
What happens when a listing is reported?
Three reports from different people hide it until OpenVibe staff look at it and restore or remove it.

faq: Do I need to open ports on my router?
No. The robot connects out to OpenVibe, and video and controls travel over WebRTC, so it works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.
Is it only for streaming?
No. Streaming is optional. Bot is a control panel for your robot first: drive it, check on it, share it and automate it.
Which robot comes first?

The Adeept 4WD Smart Car Kit for Raspberry Pi: four motors, a pan-tilt camera, distance and line sensors, lights and a buzzer. OpenVibe's device agent drives it directly, so its own open control port never has to be exposed.
Does it work with Cozmo?

Yes, built in. Cozmo makes its own Wi-Fi and runs closed firmware, so the OpenVibe agent runs on a computer next to it (a Raspberry Pi or a laptop) that joins Cozmo's Wi-Fi and stays online through another connection. You get driving, the head and lift, its camera, its face display, its voice, lights and cubes, and it stops at edges on its own. No phone app needed.
What hardware works?
A Raspberry Pi or another Linux board, an ESP32, a ROS 2 robot, an Android phone, or an ONVIF or RTSP camera. The curated kits list exactly what to buy.
How does it keep the robot safe?
The device stops its motors by itself when commands or the connection stop. There is an emergency stop in the panel, limits on speed, range and time, and every command is logged.
What will it cost?
Controlling your own robot will not cost anything. Limits and any paid extras will be published before launch.

faq: What can I watch today?
A web page (all of it, or the part a CSS selector or a pattern picks), an RSS or Atom feed (for example a GitHub releases feed), or a JSON API and a path into it.
How often does it check?
Every 15 minutes, hourly, every 6 hours or daily — your choice. It never checks faster than that, backs off when a site fails, and waits when a site asks it to.
How will I hear about a change?
When your condition fires, a notification arrives on your OpenVibe account, and the watch page shows every check and the value it found.
Does it hammer the sites it watches?
No. It sends the site's own validators first, so an unchanged page costs no body, keeps a minimum gap between requests to one site, and records every check.
Is it free?
Yes, while it is in alpha.

faq: Is this like OpenRouter?
Yes, for agents: one API and one bill for many agent systems, with live prices and rankings. Actor routes whole tasks rather than single model calls, and it checks the results before you get them.
Which agent systems does it use?
OpenVibe's own runtime, hosted agent platforms from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, coding agents, and open-source agents on OpenVibe's hardware. Each is an adapter, so new ones join quickly.
How does it choose?
For each kind of task it compares price, speed, success rate and current health across agent systems, then applies your mode and budget. Every choice is recorded and explained.
Can I keep my data on OpenVibe?
Yes. Private mode uses only OpenVibe's own runtime and open models on its own hardware.
Can it act without asking?
Only as far as you allow. Anything with consequences, like publishing, spending or moving a robot, waits for your approval, and every action is logged.
Can an agent take full control of my computer?

Only if you set that Node to Full control on the device itself. It is time-boxed and recorded, you can see when an agent is in control, and a button, a hotkey or one command ends it. Most people use Trusted: routine actions run and risky ones ask first.
Can I run Actor myself?

Yes. The router, the runtime, the console and the Node are open source and run on your own server with local models, and can link to openvibe.actor when you want hosted agents or the rest of the network.
What will it cost?
You will be able to start without paying, within limits published before launch; bigger tasks and stronger agents will be paid, with the cost shown per task.
